quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must stop completely and let others go first.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and let others go first if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and let others go first if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means you must yield. Slow down as you approach the intersection and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light mean?

options.text: Go.
Let other cars go first.
Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much alcohol you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your body weight. It is not affected by your physical fitness or how well you can handle alcohol.

questions.question: Which statement about driving on wet roads is true?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
As you slow down, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less grip your tires have. If you go too fast, your tires will lose contact with the road and you will hydroplane (slide on a layer of water).

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is starting.
A steep hill is ahead.
The bridge overhead is low.
Two lanes of traffic are merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge overhead is low.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the bridge ahead has low clearance. Do not go through if your vehicle is taller than the height shown (13 feet, 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly through the intersection.
You must stop, then go when it is safe.
You must stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
You may turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must come to a complete stop. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Signs may change this rule.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold medicine
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your driving. This includes illegal drugs, prescription medicines, and over-the-counter medicines. It is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug.

questions.question: What do five-sided signs indicate?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Five-sided signs warn you that you are in a school zone. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians.

questions.question: You cannot pass on either side of a ____ center line.

options.text: Solid and broken yellow combined
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line down the middle of a road means traffic from both directions cannot cross it to pass.

questions.question: When driving in a roundabout, you should:

options.text: Stop inside the roundabout.
Let cars entering go first.
Go clockwise around the center.
Let cars already in the roundabout go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let cars already in the roundabout go first.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with no traffic light. Traffic flows counterclockwise around a center island. Enter from the right, let traffic already in the roundabout go first, and follow the circle until you reach your exit.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.
Vehicles moving in any direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow points. You can only go if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: You have done as much as you can.
You must stay until the police arrive.
You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
You may leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car and cannot find the owner, you must leave a written note. Include your name, your address, and details about the accident.

questions.question: What affects how much space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
The presence of a stop sign.
Using your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They may drive so poorly that they appear drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may drive so poorly that they appear drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they appear to be drunk. Opening a window, turning on the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough. A drowsy driver cannot react safely to road hazards.

questions.question: You do not have to stop for a flashing red school bus on a private road.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and the stop arm out. This law applies on both public and private roads.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
Defending yourself by passing poor drivers in traffic.
Following the car ahead of you closely.
Quickly changing lanes and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you spot dangerous situations before they become accidents. This helps you avoid problems caused by aggressive, careless, or drunk drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: When can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you are riding in the back seat.
If you are riding in the back of a pickup truck.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have any open alcohol in a vehicle on a public road. You cannot drink alcohol anywhere in the vehicle, even if you are not driving.

questions.question: Should you use low beam headlights when driving in fog?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Always use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and can blind you.

questions.question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow line to pass another car?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the car ahead is driving below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing. You cannot cross them to pass another car. You can only cross double yellow lines to turn into a driveway or business entrance.

questions.question: You see or hear an emergency vehicle on a divided multilane highway. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, slow down, move your car to clear the path, and stop. Do not try to drive faster than the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should slow to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: A "Reduced speed" sign tells you to slow down. If a new speed limit is shown on the sign, that speed limit begins right at that sign.

questions.question: You reach an intersection blocked by traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move slowly until traffic ahead clears.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Do not enter the intersection until traffic clears and you can drive all the way through.
Honk your horn to make cars move ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection until traffic clears and you can drive all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if you cannot drive completely through it. Wait until traffic ahead moves so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: An eight-sided sign is always a:

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs are always stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When you park on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the side of the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves to the right and then to the left.
The road ahead curves to the left and then to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves to the right and then to the left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns that the road curves right and then left.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is one who:

options.text: Looks at objects off the road or daydreams while driving.
Makes eye contact with passengers while driving.
Only watches the vehicle directly in front of them.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, looking for things in your car, reading materials, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Keep watching the road, check your mirrors often, and look at your gauges regularly. These safe habits will help you stay focused while driving.

questions.question: Only authorized emergency or maintenance vehicles can have blue lights, flashing lights, or strobe lights.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Blue lights, flashing lights, and strobe lights are only for authorized emergency and maintenance vehicles.

questions.question: Driving while distracted:

options.text: Is never dangerous.
Usually slows your reaction time to hazards.
Usually makes you drive faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually slows your reaction time to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow your ability to react to traffic and hazards on the road. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, pulling from a curb, or entering traffic is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not needed if you use your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots before changing lanes by looking over your shoulder. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Drives slowly at all times.
Watches what other drivers are doing.
Drives at a constant speed.
Only drives in areas they know.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: Even experienced drivers can get distracted. A good defensive driver watches what other drivers do and expects potential problems.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Keep the car straight and slow down by releasing the gas pedal.
Keep your speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slow down by releasing the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Release the gas pedal and do not brake until you have control. Once the car is stable, brake gently and move to a safe spot off the road.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus unloading children, you should:

options.text: Wait until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus, watch for children walking on the side of the road. Drive carefully in areas with children.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter driving requires extra caution. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly. Snow tires help your vehicle grip the road better.

questions.question: When approaching a roundabout, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Keep your speed the same.
Slow down.
Stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching a roundabout. Roundabouts are designed for low-speed driving. You may not need to stop if no vehicles or pedestrians are in the roundabout.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to drivers who arrived before you.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to drivers who arrived before you. Wait your turn to enter the intersection.

questions.question: Before backing up your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check behind your vehicle before getting in.
Only use your mirrors.
Back up quickly.
Only look to the sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind your vehicle before getting in.
questions.explanation: Check behind your vehicle before getting in. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking your rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal 3 to 5 seconds before turning. Check your rearview mirror as you slow down. On a multilane road, move into the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then turn when it is clear.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection, the light turns yellow. Your best action is to:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Brake hard to stop.
Be ready to stop in the center of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Be prepared to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign warns of:

options.text: A road hazard.
An interstate route.
A school crossing.
A speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road hazard.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are usually yellow with warning information. They alert you to hazards or areas where special rules apply.
